title: Geometric regularity over a directed union of subfields
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $(k_i)_{i\in I}$ be a nonempty family of subfields of $k$ which is directed (for $i,j\in I$ there is $l\in I$ with $k_i\cup k_j\subseteq k_l$) and has union $k=\bigcup_ik_i$. Let $A$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] $k$-algebra, regarded as a $k_i$-algebra by restriction along $k_i\subseteq k$. If $A$ is geometrically regular over $k_i$ for every $i\in I$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202) and its proof. The proof as written has a misprint: '$k_i = k \otimes_{k_i} k_i'$' must read '$k' = k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$' (a finite purely inseparable $k'/k$ descends to a finite purely inseparable $k_i'/k_i$ with $k'\cong k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$, so $A\otimes_kk'\cong A\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$).

proof.text: *Step 1 (a finite presentation of $k'$).* By the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], since $A$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, it suffices to show that $k'\otimes_kA$ is regular for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; fix one. Choose a $k$-basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ of $k'$ ($n=\dim_kk'<\infty$). The $k$-algebra map $\pi:P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to k'$, $x_j\mapsto e_j$, is surjective, since its image is a $k$-subspace containing the basis. The field $k$ is a Noetherian ring (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $P$ is a $k$-algebra of finite type, so $P$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and $\ker\pi=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ for finitely many $f_1,\dots,f_m\in P$. Hence $k'\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ as $k$-algebras. (Stacks: 'We can get $k'$ by adjoining finitely many variables to $k$ and imposing finitely many polynomial relations.')

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202), proof, first two sentences; Definition Tag 0382

proof.text: *Step 2 (the relations are defined over some $k_i$).* The polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_m$ have finitely many coefficients $c_1,\dots,c_N\in k=\bigcup_ik_i$; choose $i_s$ with $c_s\in k_{i_s}$. As the family is nonempty and directed, induction on $N$ gives one $i\in I$ with $k_{i_s}\subseteq k_i$ for all $s$, so every $f_j$ lies in $P_i=k_i[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subseteq P$. Put $J_i=(f_1,\dots,f_m)\subseteq P_i$ and $k_i'=P_i/J_i$, a commutative $k_i$-algebra.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG proof, third sentence ('there exists an $i$ and ... $k_i'/k_i$')

proof.text: *Step 3 ($k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'\cong k'$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=k_i$, $S=P_i$, the $S$-algebra $P_i/J_i$ and the $R$-algebra $k$) and symmetry of $\otimes$, $k\otimes_{k_i}(P_i/J_i)\cong(P_i/J_i)\otimes_{P_i}(P_i\otimes_{k_i}k)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=k_i$, $R=k$) $P_i\otimes_{k_i}k\cong k\otimes_{k_i}k_i[x_1,\dots,x_n]\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]=P$, $p\otimes c\mapsto cp$, a map of $P_i$-algebras for the inclusion $P_i\subseteq P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=P_i$, $B=P$, $I=J_i$) $P\otimes_{P_i}(P_i/J_i)\cong P/J_iP=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$, which is $k'$ by step 1. Following $c\otimes1$ ($c\in k$) through these maps, it goes to $c$, so the composite $\theta:k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'\xrightarrow{\sim}k'$ is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras, $k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$ being a $k$-algebra via $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. (This is the identity '$k'=k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$' of the Stacks proof, printed there as '$k_i=k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG proof, third sentence (with the misprint '$k_i$' for '$k'$' corrected)

proof.text: *Step 4 ($k_i'/k_i$ is finite purely inseparable).* By step 3, $k\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$ is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to $k'$, so it is a field and, via $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, a finite purely inseparable field extension of $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-scalar-descent] (with $K=k_i$, $L=k$, $B=k_i'$), $k_i'$ is a field and a finite purely inseparable field extension of $k_i$ via $k_i\to P_i/J_i$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG proof, third sentence ('a finite purely inseparable field extension $k_i'/k_i$')

proof.text: *Step 5 (conclusion).* The $k$-algebra isomorphism $\theta$ of step 3 gives a ring isomorphism $A\otimes_kk'\cong A\otimes_k(k\otimes_{k_i}k_i')$, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=k_i$, $S=k$, the $S$-algebra $A$ and the $R$-algebra $k_i'$) gives $A\otimes_k(k\otimes_{k_i}k_i')\cong A\otimes_{k_i}k_i'$, $a\otimes(c\otimes y)\mapsto ca\otimes y$, where $A$ is a $k_i$-algebra by restriction along $k_i\subseteq k$ as in the statement. With symmetry of $\otimes$, $k'\otimes_kA\cong k_i'\otimes_{k_i}A$ as rings. Since $A$ is geometrically regular over $k_i$ and $k_i'/k_i$ is finite purely inseparable (step 4), $k_i'\otimes_{k_i}A$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; being Noetherian with regular local rings at all primes is preserved by ring isomorphisms, so $k'\otimes_kA$ is regular. As $k'/k$ was arbitrary and $A$ is Noetherian, $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].
